# Renault Master Immobiliser Stays Off, Engine Cranks But Won't Fire

A common failure mode in automotive electronics, particularly when a vehicle sits dormant for months, is the decoupling of the immobilizer transponder system from the engine control unit (ECU). In the specific case of a 2003 Renault Master where the dashboard indicator light between STOP and SERV remains dark despite ignition attempts, the root cause is almost certainly not a mechanical failure of the starter motor or fuel pump. Instead, this points to a logic error in the anti-theft handshake.

When you turn the key, the ECU requires proof that the driver possesses the authorized key before enabling fuel injection and ignition spark. The little red dot you expect to see is the visual confirmation that the transponder chip inside the ignition cylinder has been read and verified. If this light stays off while all other dash lights illuminate, the ECU has likely entered a "no-start" safety mode because it never received the correct cryptographic challenge-response from the key.

The most probable culprit here is a dead or failing transponder coil (the antenna ring wrapped around the ignition barrel). After four months of inactivity, parasitic drain or minor corrosion can sometimes affect low-voltage circuits. However, the issue isn't necessarily power loss to the light itself; it's a lack of signal. The coil needs sufficient voltage to generate the magnetic field that powers the passive RFID chip inside your key. If the coil is open circuit or its resistance has drifted out of spec, the ECU reads "no key present" and cuts fuel immediately upon cranking.

To diagnose this without replacing parts blindly, you can perform a continuity test on the immobilizer system wiring if the service manual for the D7 engine (common in that era Master) is accessible. Locate the connector for the immobilizer coil near the steering column. Disconnect it and measure resistance with a multimeter. Values typically fall between 200 and 800 ohms depending on the specific Renault generation. An infinite reading indicates an open coil, which explains why the light never turns on: the circuit is broken before the ECU can even attempt to read the chip.

Another possibility involves the ignition lock cylinder itself. The mechanical tumblers inside the lock often house a small reed switch or a contact point that closes only when the key is fully inserted and turned to the "ON" position. If these contacts are corroded or worn, the ECU may not detect the "start" command at all, or it fails to trigger the immobilizer light logic. In some Renault architectures of this period, the immobilizer light is tied directly to the ignition switch micro-switches rather than being an independent status LED controlled by the ECU. If the switch contacts are pitted, the light won't engage even if the key code is valid.

If you have a spare key known to work on another vehicle, swapping it into the Master will immediately isolate whether the fault lies with the current transponder chip or the ignition barrel. If the second key triggers the light and starts the engine, the original transponder has failed or its internal memory has been corrupted, possibly due to exposure to moisture during the long period of disuse.

There is also a distinct chance that the ECU itself has entered a protective state where it refuses to start without a fresh immobilizer handshake sequence. Some Renault ECUs require a specific diagnostic session to reset the security counter if they detect repeated failed attempts or a persistent lack of signal. Without connecting to a compatible OBD-II scanner capable of accessing the immobilizer module, you might be stuck in an infinite loop of cranking and dying.

In many cases, replacing the ignition barrel assembly resolves this immediately because it contains both the mechanical lock and the electrical contacts for the immobilizer coil. Since the vehicle sits unused, corrosion on these delicate contacts is a very high-probability event. Before stripping the steering column to replace the entire unit, verify the resistance of the existing coil connector. If the wiring integrity holds but the light remains dark, the ignition cylinder assembly is the definitive fix.
